```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(slider)
library(here)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)

source(here("R", "qc_functions.R"))
source(here("R", "station_qc.R"))
source(here("R", "qc_report_functions.R"))

# Summaries of every stored QC result (run-qc.R writes them to data/qc/). Reading ten stations of
# 15-minute data takes a minute or two.
tabs <- qc_report_tables()

region_order <- c("SJR corridor", "South Delta", "Export intakes", "Central Delta", "West Delta", "Sacramento River", "Delta gateway", "Suisun Bay")
regions <- read_csv(here("data", "station_screening.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  transmute(series = station, region = str_replace(region, " \\(.*\\)", ""))
series_levels <- tibble(series = names(qc_jobs)) |>
  left_join(regions, by = "series") |>
  mutate(region = replace_na(region, "SJR corridor"),                         # RRI_cdec_2026
         region = factor(region, levels = region_order)) |>
  arrange(region, match(series, names(qc_jobs))) |>
  pull(series)
series_label <- function(s) if_else(s == "RRI_cdec_2026", "RRI (CDEC 2026)", s)
lab_levels <- series_label(series_levels)
fct_series <- function(s) factor(series_label(s), levels = rev(lab_levels))     # first station at the top

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
                                                legend.title.position = "top"))
pct1 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
```

```{r}
#| label: derived
out <- tabs$outcome |>
  mutate(label = qc_outcome_label(outcome),
         source = if_else(series == "RRI_cdec_2026", "provisional", source))   # the CDEC file is provisional by design

# Three groups of outcomes
passed  <- c("Valid", "Corroborated event (kept)")
removed <- c("Isolated spike (removed)", "Gross range (removed)")
review  <- c("Uncorroborated excursion", "Flat line", "Erratic period")

by_series <- out |>
  group_by(series) |>
  summarise(rows = sum(n),
            no_value = sum(n[label == "No turbidity value"]),
            screened = rows - no_value,
            passed = sum(n[label %in% passed]),
            removed = sum(n[label %in% removed]),
            review = sum(n[label %in% review]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tabs$scope |> select(series, first, last, expected_rows, provisional_rows), by = "series") |>
  mutate(across(c(passed, removed, review), ~ 100 * .x / screened, .names = "pct_{.col}"),
         pct_no_value = 100 * no_value / rows,
         pct_flagged = pct_removed + pct_review)

tot <- by_series |> summarise(rows = sum(rows), screened = sum(screened), passed = sum(passed),
                              removed = sum(removed), review = sum(review), no_value = sum(no_value))

ev <- tabs$events |> mutate(label = qc_outcome_label(outcome))
n_events_review <- ev |> filter(label %in% review) |> count(series, name = "review_events")
```

## At a glance

- **`r format(tot$rows, big.mark = ",")` readings** from **`r nrow(by_series)` series** (`r format(min(by_series$first))` to `r format(max(by_series$last))`) went through the QC screen. `r format(tot$screened, big.mark = ",")` had a turbidity value to test; the other `r pct1(100 * tot$no_value / tot$rows)` are blank in the sonde files.
- **`r pct1(100 * tot$passed / tot$screened)` passed** every test. **`r pct1(100 * tot$removed / tot$screened)` were removed** (isolated spikes and impossible values, set to missing in the final series) and **`r pct1(100 * tot$review / tot$screened)` were flagged for review** (kept in the data, left out of the analysis series).
- The station with the largest share of flagged or removed readings is **`r series_label(by_series$series[which.max(by_series$pct_flagged)])`** (`r pct1(max(by_series$pct_flagged))`); the cleanest is **`r series_label(by_series$series[which.min(by_series$pct_flagged)])`** (`r pct1(min(by_series$pct_flagged))`).
- **`r format(sum(n_events_review$review_events), big.mark = ",")` events** (runs of consecutive flagged readings) are waiting for a person to look at them. The longest are listed in [the review queue](#review-queue).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-glance
#| tbl-cap: "Outcome of the screen by series. Percentages of readings with a turbidity value, except 'No value', which is a share of all rows."
by_series |>
  left_join(n_events_review, by = "series") |>
  transmute(Series = series_label(series), From = format(first, "%Y-%m"), To = format(last, "%Y-%m"),
            `Rows` = format(rows, big.mark = ","), `No value` = pct1(pct_no_value),
            `Screened` = format(screened, big.mark = ","), `Passed` = pct1(pct_passed),
            `Removed` = pct1(pct_removed), `Flagged for review` = pct1(pct_review),
            `Review events` = replace_na(review_events, 0L)) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrrrrrrr")
```

## How the readings fared

```{r}
#| label: fig-outcome
#| fig-cap: "Share of screened readings that were removed or flagged, by station and reason. Stations are ordered by the total. Readings that passed (about 97-100%) are not drawn."
#| fig-height: 9
order_lvls <- by_series |> arrange(pct_flagged) |> pull(series) |> series_label()
out |>
  filter(!label %in% c(passed, "No turbidity value")) |>
  group_by(series, label) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(by_series |> select(series, screened), by = "series") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / screened, Station = factor(series_label(series), levels = order_lvls)) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, Station, fill = label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = by_series |> mutate(Station = factor(series_label(series), levels = order_lvls)),
            aes(pct_flagged, Station, label = pct1(pct_flagged), fill = NULL), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = qc_outcome_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12)), labels = label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(x = "Share of screened readings", y = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-heat-flagged
#| fig-cap: "Share of screened readings removed or flagged, by station and year. Dark cells are where to look first: a bad deployment, a fouled sensor or a stretch of erratic data."
#| fig-height: 10
out |>
  filter(label != "No turbidity value") |>
  group_by(series, year) |>
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(n[label %in% c(removed, review)]) / sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Station = fct_series(series)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), Station, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(pct >= 1, sprintf("%.0f", pct), "")), size = 2.9, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt", name = "% flagged\nor removed",
                       breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 20, 50), labels = label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Data coverage: share of the 15-minute readings in each year that have a turbidity value. Gaps are missing sensor output, not QC decisions."
#| fig-height: 10
tabs$scope |>
  select(series, first, last) |>
  cross_join(tibble(year = 2005:max(year(tabs$scope$last)))) |>
  mutate(start = pmax(as_date(paste0(year, "-01-01")), first), end = pmin(as_date(paste0(year, "-12-31")), last),
         days = as.numeric(end - start) + 1) |>
  filter(days > 0) |>
  left_join(out |> filter(label != "No turbidity value") |> group_by(series, year) |> summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("series", "year")) |>
  mutate(coverage = 100 * replace_na(n, 0) / (96 * days), Station = fct_series(series)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), Station, fill = coverage)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", coverage)), size = 2.7, colour = "grey15") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F6D9D2", high = "#2E86AB", limits = c(0, 100), name = "Coverage",
                      labels = label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
```

## Which sensors produce the most out-of-range values

Every parameter on a sonde gets a range screen (physically impossible for the sensor or the river, such as pH of 277 or a 9999 code). Only turbidity gets the outlier, erratic-period and flat-line tests (see [Methods](#methods)), so for the other parameters this is the full extent of the screen.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sensors
#| fig-cap: "Range-screen failures per 100,000 readings, by station and sensor (all years). Numbers are the count of failed readings. Grey cells: the station does not report that parameter."
#| fig-height: 9
sens <- tabs$params |>
  group_by(series, param) |>
  summarise(measured = sum(measured), fail = sum(range_fail), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(qc_params |> select(param, label), by = "param") |>
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * fail / pmax(measured, 1), Station = fct_series(series),
         label = factor(label, levels = qc_params$label))
ggplot(sens, aes(label, Station, fill = if_else(measured == 0, NA_real_, rate))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(measured == 0, "", format(fail, big.mark = ","))), size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FFF3E0", high = "#B23A00", trans = "sqrt", na.value = "grey90",
                      name = "per 100,000\nreadings", labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1), legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensors
#| tbl-cap: "Readings reported and range failures by sensor, all stations combined."
sens |>
  group_by(Sensor = label) |>
  summarise(Stations = sum(measured > 0), Readings = sum(measured), `Range failures` = sum(fail),
            `Per 100,000` = round(1e5 * sum(fail) / sum(measured), 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(c(Readings, `Range failures`), ~ format(.x, big.mark = ","))) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

## Events: when and where the trouble was {#events}

An *event* is a run of consecutive readings with the same flag. Isolated spikes (one or two readings) are numerous and are counted in the figures above; this timeline shows the longer disturbances, which are the ones that can bias a seasonal or annual comparison.

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Flagged events lasting at least 3 hours (isolated spikes excluded). Point size is the event duration; colour is the flag."
#| fig-height: 9
ev |>
  filter(label %in% c(review, "Corroborated event (kept)"), hours >= 3) |>
  mutate(Station = fct_series(series)) |>
  ggplot(aes(start, Station)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = hours, colour = label), alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, breaks = c(6, 24, 24 * 7, 24 * 30), labels = c("6 h", "1 day", "1 week", "1 month"),
                  name = "Duration") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = qc_outcome_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 4)), size = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-season
#| fig-cap: "Share of screened readings removed or flagged by calendar month, all years. A seasonal pattern points to something real (storms, vessel traffic, algal blooms, summer fouling) rather than random sensor faults."
#| fig-height: 9
out |>
  filter(label != "No turbidity value") |>
  group_by(series, month) |>
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(n[label %in% c(removed, review)]) / sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Station = fct_series(series), Month = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb)) |>
  ggplot(aes(Month, Station, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", pct)), size = 2.9, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt", name = "% flagged\nor removed",
                       breaks = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5), labels = label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"))
```

### Is the sensor the same through time?

A change of sensor, or of how the data were processed, can look like a change in the water. This view shows how jumpy each station's turbidity is from year to year. The step rises and falls with turbidity itself (a wet year is noisier than a dry one), so the thing to look for is a step in noise that comes with no change in the median level. Chipps Island (MAL) is the clear case: its step is about 2 in 2008-2010, about 6 in 2011-2024, and 0.7 in 2025, with a median level of 13-14 in both 2024 and 2025, while its neighbours do not change. The old Old River, Middle River and Tracy stations (MHO, OH1, TWA, MRU) show a smaller drop in 2004-2005. Check the deployment logs for sensor swaps before using a station's record across a change.

```{r}
#| label: fig-noise
#| fig-cap: "Typical size of the 15-minute step in turbidity, by year, relative to each station's own median across years (colour: red = noisier than usual, blue = quieter). Numbers are the median step in FNU/NTU. A sudden change in one station, with its neighbours unchanged, points to a different sensor or different processing."
#| fig-height: 10
tabs$noise |>
  group_by(series) |>
  mutate(rel = log2(noise / median(noise))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(readings >= 5000) |>
  mutate(Station = fct_series(series)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), Station, fill = pmax(pmin(rel, 3), -3))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = if_else(noise >= 10, sprintf("%.0f", noise), sprintf("%.2f", noise))), size = 2.3, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2C7BB6", mid = "white", high = "#D7191C", midpoint = 0, name = "vs station median",
                       breaks = c(-3, -1.58, 0, 1.58, 3), labels = c("1/8", "1/3", "same", "3x", "8x")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5), legend.key.width = unit(1.3, "cm"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-provisional
#| fig-cap: "Flag rate in the QC'd record versus the provisional CDEC readings (real-time, no field QC) appended to it. The provisional readings cover only 2026, so a single event can dominate a station's rate."
#| fig-height: 8
prov <- out |>
  filter(label != "No turbidity value") |>
  group_by(series, source) |>
  summarise(pct = 100 * sum(n[label %in% c(removed, review)]) / sum(n), n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Station = fct_series(series), Source = recode(source, primary = "QC'd record", provisional = "Provisional CDEC"))
ggplot(prov, aes(pct, Station, fill = Source)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single"), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("QC'd record" = "#7A8B99", "Provisional CDEC" = "#E69F00"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)), labels = label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  labs(x = "Share of screened readings removed or flagged", y = NULL)
```

## What changed recently {#recent}

Each station's last 12 months compared with its own history: months whose share of removed or flagged readings is at or above the station's 95th percentile of all months. A station creeping upward over several months is the pattern of a fouling or failing sensor.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recent
#| tbl-cap: "Months in the last 12 whose removed-or-flagged share is in the top 5% of that station's own record (months with at least 1,000 screened readings)."
monthly <- out |>
  filter(label != "No turbidity value") |>
  group_by(series, year, month) |>
  summarise(screened = sum(n), pct = 100 * sum(n[label %in% c(removed, review)]) / sum(n),
            spikes = 100 * sum(n[label == "Isolated spike (removed)"]) / sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(screened >= 1000) |>
  mutate(month_start = make_date(year, month, 1)) |>
  group_by(series) |>
  mutate(typical = median(pct), pctile = ecdf(pct)(pct), p95 = quantile(pct, 0.95)) |>
  ungroup()
latest <- max(monthly$month_start)
recent <- monthly |> filter(month_start > latest %m-% months(12), pct >= p95, pct > 0.5)
if (nrow(recent) == 0) {
  cat("No station has a month in the last 12 that is unusually high for its own record.\n")
} else {
  recent |>
    arrange(series, month_start) |>
    transmute(Station = series_label(series), Month = format(month_start, "%Y-%m"), `Screened` = format(screened, big.mark = ","),
              `Removed or flagged` = pct1(pct), `of which isolated spikes` = pct1(spikes),
              `Station's typical month` = pct1(typical)) |>
    kable(align = "llrrrr")
}
```

## Review queue {#review-queue}

The longest events flagged for review. These stay in the data; they are only left out of the analysis series. The baseline is the median of the valid readings in the 24 hours before the event.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-queue
#| tbl-cap: "The 25 longest events flagged for review."
ev |>
  filter(label %in% review) |>
  arrange(desc(hours)) |>
  slice_head(n = 25) |>
  transmute(Station = series_label(series), Flag = label, Start = format(start, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
            Days = round(hours / 24, 1), `Peak (FNU/NTU)` = round(peak_fnu, 1),
            `Median in event` = round(median_fnu, 1), `Baseline before` = round(baseline_fnu, 1)) |>
  kable(align = "llrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spikes
#| tbl-cap: "The 15 largest isolated spikes that were removed (peak relative to the baseline before)."
ev |>
  filter(label == "Isolated spike (removed)", is.finite(peak_fnu)) |>
  arrange(desc(peak_fnu)) |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  transmute(Station = series_label(series), Time = format(start, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
            Readings = n_readings, `Peak (FNU/NTU)` = round(peak_fnu, 1), `Baseline before` = round(baseline_fnu, 1)) |>
  kable(align = "llrrr")
```

### Could excursions be corroborated?

A sustained turbidity excursion is kept as a real event if conductivity or dissolved oxygen shifts at the same time (a storm, a tidal intrusion). Stations that report turbidity only (the CDEC downloads) cannot pass that test, so their excursions are flagged by construction.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corroboration
#| tbl-cap: "Sustained excursions (more than two consecutive outlier readings) and whether a second channel was available."
tabs$corroboration |>
  filter(excursion_readings > 0) |>
  transmute(Station = series_label(series), `Excursion readings` = excursion_readings,
            `With conductivity or DO` = pct1(100 * with_channels / excursion_readings),
            `Corroborated` = pct1(100 * corroborated / excursion_readings)) |>
  kable(align = "lrrr")
```

## Station detail

For each station: the daily median of the final turbidity series (log scale), with a marker on each day that had removed or flagged readings, placed at the day's peak reading. The lower panel zooms to the last two years.

```{r}
#| label: station-fn
drawn <- c("Isolated spike (removed)", "Gross range (removed)", "Uncorroborated excursion", "Flat line", "Erratic period")
station_plot <- function(s) {
  d <- tabs$daily |> filter(series == s, !is.na(median_final))
  f <- tabs$flag_days |> filter(series == s, is.finite(peak_fnu), peak_fnu > 0) |> mutate(label = qc_outcome_label(outcome))
  lim <- drawn[drawn %in% as.character(f$label)]            # legend lists only the flag types this station has
  if (length(lim) == 0) lim <- drawn[1]
  base <- function(d, f) {
    ggplot() +
      geom_line(data = d, aes(date, median_final), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.35) +
      geom_point(data = f, aes(date, peak_fnu, colour = label), size = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = qc_outcome_colours[lim], limits = lim, name = NULL) +
      scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Turbidity (FNU/NTU)")
  }
  leg <- guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)))
  p1 <- base(d, f) + labs(title = paste(series_label(s), "- full record"))
  if (as.numeric(max(d$date) - min(d$date)) < 800) return(p1 + leg)
  from <- max(d$date) - 730
  p2 <- base(filter(d, date >= from), filter(f, date >= from)) + labs(title = "Last two years") + leg
  p1 <- p1 + theme(legend.position = "none")       # one legend, under the lower panel
  p1 / p2
}
```

```{r}
#| label: station-tabs
#| results: asis
tmpl <- c("### {{s}}", "", "```{r}", "#| echo: false", "#| fig-height: 6.4", "station_plot('{{s}}')", "```", "")
cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
cat(unlist(lapply(series_levels, function(s) knitr::knit_child(text = knitr::knit_expand(text = tmpl, s = s), quiet = TRUE))), sep = "\n")
cat(":::\n")
```

## Methods {#methods}

This is the *secondary* screen. It runs after the field-based primary QC (Wagner et al. 2006 method), and it catches residual statistical outliers rather than redoing field QC. **Nothing is deleted:** every reading stays in the stored files with a `qaqc_flag` and the flag column of each step. Settings below are read from the functions in `R/qc_functions.R`, so the table always matches the code that ran.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-methods
f1 <- formals(check_gross_range); f2 <- formals(flag_robust_outliers); f3 <- formals(flag_erratic_periods)
f4 <- formals(flag_flat_lines); f5 <- formals(classify_run_duration); f6 <- formals(corroborate_sustained_excursions)
tribble(
  ~Step, ~`What it catches`, ~Setting, ~Outcome,
  "Gross range", "Turbidity outside the sensor's physical range",
    sprintf("%g to %g FNU", f1$min_val, f1$max_val), "Removed",
  "Parameter ranges", "Impossible temperature, pH, conductivity, DO, chlorophyll (error codes, failed sensors)",
    "see table below", "Value set to missing in the <parameter>_qc column",
  "Robust outlier", "A reading far from its neighbours (rolling median and MAD, modified z-score)",
    sprintf("+/-%d readings (%g h); |z| > %g and more than %g FNU from the median", f2$window, f2$window / 4, f2$z_thresh, f2$noise_floor),
    "Candidate: classified next",
  "Isolated spike", "An outlier run that returns to baseline at once",
    sprintf("%d readings or fewer (%g min)", f5$max_spike_len, 15 * f5$max_spike_len), "Removed",
  "Sustained excursion", "An outlier run longer than a spike",
    sprintf("kept if conductivity or DO also shifts (|z| > %g), otherwise flagged", f6$corrob_z_thresh),
    "Kept as a real event, or flagged for review",
  "Erratic period", "A long stretch of jumpy data that the rolling window cannot see",
    sprintf("median 15-min change over +/-%g h exceeds %g FNU (Chipps Island and Suisun Bay stations: ten times the station's typical step instead, see qc_summary.csv)", f3$window / 4, f3$jump_thresh), "Flagged for review",
  "Flat line", "A stuck sensor repeating one value",
    sprintf("%d or more identical readings (%g h), plus %d readings either side", f4$min_run, f4$min_run / 4, f4$pad_readings),
    "Flagged for review"
) |> kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-limits
#| tbl-cap: "Range limits used by the parameter screen. Brackish tidal stations (TWI, ANH, BLP) get a higher conductivity ceiling."
limit_tbl <- function(l) imap_dfr(l, ~ tibble(Parameter = .y, Low = .x[1], High = .x[2]))
left_join(limit_tbl(param_limits), limit_tbl(tidal_cond) |> rename(`Low (tidal)` = Low, `High (tidal)` = High), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(`Low (tidal)` = if_else(`Low (tidal)` == Low & `High (tidal)` == High, NA_real_, `Low (tidal)`),
         `High (tidal)` = if_else(is.na(`Low (tidal)`), NA_real_, `High (tidal)`)) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

### File integrity

A parameter that rises or falls steadily with time (rank correlation with time of 0.8 or more) points to a sorted or damaged column, as in the Chipps Island (MAL) conductivity that led to that station being dropped.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-integrity
#| tbl-cap: "Parameters most strongly trending with time, by station (Spearman correlation with time). Values near 1 or -1 would mean a damaged column; moderate values are real long-term change."
tabs$integrity |>
  filter(abs(rho_time) >= 0.4) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(rho_time))) |>
  left_join(qc_params |> select(param, label), by = "param") |>
  transmute(Station = series_label(series), Parameter = label, Readings = format(n, big.mark = ","),
            `Correlation with time` = sprintf("%.2f", rho_time), Suspect = if_else(suspect, "yes", "no")) |>
  kable(align = "llrrr")
```

## Reading this report

- **A flag is not a verdict.** Vessel wakes, storms and dredging produce real turbidity pulses that look like outliers. Flagged readings are kept so that a person can decide; the "analysis" series leaves them out only because the Golden Mussel comparison is about ambient clarity.
- **Flag rates are not sensor grades.** A station with a high rate may sit in a harsher spot (shipping channel, tidal slough) rather than have a worse sonde. Compare a station with its own history (the year-by-year heat map) before comparing it with others.
- **Only turbidity is fully screened.** The other parameters have range checks, and they act as corroborating channels for turbidity. Extending the outlier, erratic and flat-line tests to them is a planned step.
- **Provisional data are different.** The 2026 CDEC readings are real-time and have had no field QC, and they carry turbidity only, so they run a stricter test (no second channel to corroborate).
- **Valid means tested and passed.** Rows where the sonde recorded nothing are counted separately as "No turbidity value" and are not in any percentage of screened readings.
